suread: review R1 素读（只读 text/，未开 md）

facts.fact: 农场每天七点半开工，赶在佛州酷热起来之前
facts.anchor: work at the farm starting at seven thirty each day, before Florida’s heat grew relentless

facts.fact: 到第二个下午她就陷进熔化般的恍惚
facts.anchor: I found myself drifting into a molten daze by my second afternoon

facts.fact: 一会儿新建电脑档案、一会儿用妈妈的话贴标签
facts.anchor: I’d be creating a new file on the computer one minute, then labeling it with Mama’s words the next

facts.fact: 第二个下午她一边建文件一边用 Mama 的话打标：The devil’s inside
facts.anchor: The devil’s inside.

facts.fact: 仍不知道 Gazzie 做了什么让母亲写下那样绝望的字句
facts.anchor: I still didn’t know what Gazzie had done to make my mother write such desperate phrases

facts.fact: 她开始为偏离了追查这件事而内疚
facts.anchor: beginning to feel guilty that I’d strayed from my quest to figure it out

facts.fact: 浓烈的新煮咖啡味把她从分拣的麻木里拉出来
facts.anchor: The acrid smell of fresh coffee drew me out of a sorting stupor

facts.fact: 纸撒到地上、她蹲下去、掌心被地毯磨烫
facts.anchor: Papers dropping to the floor, I twisted into a crouch, my palms burning from the carpet

facts.fact: 视野收窄成隧道
facts.anchor: My vision tunneled.

facts.fact: 恢复时 Harrison 已在裂开的门外
facts.anchor: Harrison had moved beyond the cracked door

facts.fact: 日光灯下他的眼是干净洗澡水的淡蓝
facts.anchor: his eyes were the pale blue of clean bathwater

facts.fact: 她不由欣赏他的穿着：公司肌肉背心加靴型牛仔裤
facts.anchor: I couldn’t help but appreciate his outfit: a Greer Fine Alligators muscle T-shirt and bootcut jeans

facts.fact: 要是穿牛仔靴就像个色情片演员
facts.anchor: If he’d worn cowboy boots, he could’ve been a porn star

facts.fact: 他一只手托着咖啡杯，把手朝她伸过来
facts.anchor: One hand cupped a coffee mug, handle extended toward me

facts.fact: 他说：想你该需要休息一下
facts.anchor: “Thought you’d appreciate a break,” he said.

facts.fact: 她回「哦？」并完全不怀疑他一秒
facts.anchor: I didn’t believe him for a second

facts.fact: 她酸答：考虑到整理档案的紧迫需要，我不确定有没有时间
facts.anchor: “I don’t know if I have time, given the pressing need to organize these files.”

facts.fact: 她明知自己在公开讽刺且不在乎
facts.anchor: I was being openly sarcastic, but I didn’t care.

facts.fact: 她的定性：Harrison 是拍祖母马屁、好让她把帝国遗赠给他的黄鼠狼
facts.anchor: Harrison was a weasel who’d sucked up to my grandmother so she’d will him her empire

facts.fact: 她自我开脱：对他语气短促并不是坏人
facts.anchor: I wasn’t a bad person for being short with him.

facts.fact: 他脸颊泛起淡粉但仍把杯子举着；说确实得整理档案、Gazzie 久已 neglect、不是爱做文书的人
facts.anchor: To my pleasure, his cheeks glowed a faint pink, but he continued to hold out the mug.

facts.fact: 她说：这就是你说服她把我和几十年没动过的箱子锁进壁橱的唯一理由
facts.anchor: That’s the only reason you convinced her to lock me in a closet with boxes that haven’t been touched for half a century.

facts.fact: 他打量她，像在决定要不要把咖啡浇在她人字拖上
facts.anchor: He studied me, like he was deciding whether to pour the coffee over my flip-flops.

facts.fact: 他把杯子再伸远些；问她要不要，half-and-half 在休息室
facts.anchor: Then he extended the cup out farther. “Do you want this or not? If you need half-and-half, it’s in the break room.”

facts.fact: 她不喝、心脏受不了；但眼皮在沉
facts.anchor: I wasn’t a coffee drinker—my heart couldn’t handle much of it—but my eyelids were drooping

facts.fact: 她想不通他为何端来、断定他必有所求
facts.anchor: I wasn’t sure why he’d brought it, though. He had to want something from me.

facts.fact: 她说「算是谢谢吧」、慢慢站起
facts.anchor: “Thanks, I guess,” I said, standing slowly.

facts.fact: 她不肯新认的仇人面前失态晕倒
facts.anchor: I wouldn’t survive the indignity of fainting in front of my newfound nemesis

facts.fact: 他身上是柔顺片的味道，原以为该是泥浆或幼鳄棚
facts.anchor: who, to my annoyance, smelled like dryer sheets. I’d expected him to smell like mud or a hatchling barn.

facts.fact: 抓杯把时他瞥见她指上的墨渍，问笔炸了？
facts.anchor: As I grabbed the mug handle, he glanced at my ink-stained fingers. “Pen burst on you?”

facts.fact: 她答：我画画
facts.anchor: When he continued to look at me expectantly, I added, “I draw.”

facts.fact: 他：真羡慕，我连圆都画不圆；随即抿嘴像吐了个大秘密
facts.anchor: “Good for you. I can’t draw a circle.” He pressed his mouth shut, like he’d spilled a terrible secret.

facts.fact: 他原没打算闲聊
facts.anchor: He must not have meant to chitchat.

facts.fact: 礼貌让他的声音发紧：你画什么？
facts.anchor: “What do you draw?” Politeness strained his voice.

facts.fact: 她答：噩梦
facts.anchor: “Nightmares.”

facts.fact: 他半笑：Greer House 也让你发毛？
facts.anchor: His mouth lifted in a half smile. “Greer House creeps you out, too?”

facts.fact: 她心想他会知道、他在那宅子里待的时间多半比她长
facts.anchor: He would know; he’d probably spent more time in it than I had.

facts.fact: 她疑他正找机会拿来呛她
facts.anchor: He’d probably been looking for a chance to rub that in my face, too.

facts.fact: 她问：你常去那儿吧？
facts.anchor: “You’re there a lot, huh?”

facts.fact: 他答 Yeah；随即问她还打算待多久
facts.anchor: Before I could muster a snarky reply, he asked, “How long do you think you’ll stay?”

facts.fact: 他想装随意，但急切爬进声音
facts.anchor: He was going for casual, but eagerness crept into his voice.

facts.fact: 她由此明白他为何端咖啡：想知道她是否要争农场、会不会挑战他
facts.anchor: So that’s why he’d brought me the coffee. He wanted to know if I was trying to inherit the farm, if I would challenge him.

facts.fact: 她决定不让他轻易得到答案
facts.anchor: I wouldn’t make it easy for him to get answers.

facts.fact: 她只答：还不确定
facts.anchor: “Not sure yet.”

facts.fact: 他：看起来至少 Gazzie 很想让她留下
facts.anchor: “Well, it seems like Gazzie, for one, really wants you to stick around.”

facts.fact: 她：他真有胆；此刻她想把自己的咖啡浇在他脚趾上
facts.anchor: He had some nerve. Now I was picturing pouring the coffee over his toes.

facts.fact: 狭窄房间里两人相距两英尺；她得仰头才对他的眼
facts.anchor: In the cramped room, we stood two feet apart. I had to tilt my head to meet his eyes.

facts.fact: 在 Greer House 他们保持距离时她没注意到他的身高
facts.anchor: In Greer House, where we’d kept our distance, I hadn’t noticed his height.

facts.fact: 这里她看出他至少高她六英寸，仰视让她更怒
facts.anchor: Here, I could tell he had at least six inches on me, and the fact I had to look up at him made me angrier.

facts.fact: 她一分钟都不愿再待在那闷热房间
facts.anchor: I couldn’t stay in that stuffy room with him one more minute.

facts.fact: 她借咖啡难喝脱身去拿 half-and-half
facts.anchor: “I guess I need half-and-half after all,” I said. “Whoever made this coffee doesn’t have taste buds.”

facts.fact: 休息室里 Nova 坐在唯一那张圆桌边
facts.anchor: In the break room, Nova sat at the single circular table.

facts.fact: Nova 的半笑在她眼光扫到身后的 Harrison 时僵住
facts.anchor: She gave me a half smile that froze in place when her eyes flicked to Harrison behind me.

facts.fact: 她像在太用力地假装对他的肱二头肌免疫
facts.anchor: She looked like she was trying a little too hard to pretend she was immune to his biceps.

facts.fact: Nova 的「Hey」是朝 Harrison 说的
facts.anchor: “Hey,” she said, addressing him.

facts.fact: Harrison 礼貌地笑一下径直走向冰箱
facts.anchor: He gave her a polite smile and continued to the fridge. “Hey yourself.”

facts.fact: 她捕捉到 Nova 脸上一丝皱眉的残影
facts.anchor: I clocked the ghost of a frown on Nova’s face as he pulled out the half-and-half and handed it to me.

facts.fact: 她的两种解释：Nova 想把 Harrison 独占／或 Nova 受命把她隔离，怕这算违规
facts.anchor: Perhaps she liked to keep Harrison to herself. That, or Gazzie had asked her to keep me isolated in my filing cave and she worried this constituted a breach.

facts.fact: Harrison 靠着台面问她期待在农场做什么；叙述者说他决心黏着不放
facts.anchor: The man was determined to hover.

facts.fact: 她嗤之以鼻、想起第一次晚餐上 Gazzie 的审问
facts.anchor: I scoffed, remembering Gazzie’s interrogation during our first dinner.

facts.fact: 他耸肩直说：你说得对，你什么都不知道
facts.anchor: He shrugged. “You’re right. You don’t.”

facts.fact: 她拒绝上钩，改打量他能有什么用处、盘算骗他多带她看农场
facts.anchor: I refused to take the bait. Instead, I eyed him. He had to be useful somehow.

facts.fact: 她判断他是那种会吃「落难女子」一套的人
facts.anchor: He seemed the type who would appreciate a damsel in distress.

facts.fact: 她的示弱表演：换成我也不会让陌生人在生意里乱走
facts.anchor: I guess I wouldn’t let a stranger run loose around my business, either

facts.fact: 她搬出「Florida Man Brings Farm Gator to Local Bar」的新闻句式
facts.anchor: ‘Florida Man Brings Farm Gator to Local Bar.’

facts.fact: 她装作突然冒出天真念头：或许他能带她转转
facts.anchor: I paused, like I’d suddenly had an innocent idea. “Maybe you could show me around?”

facts.fact: 他反问：她不是带你参观过了？
facts.anchor: “Didn’t she already take you on a tour?”

facts.fact: 她答：只看了外面，里面没看到
facts.anchor: “Outside. I didn’t get to see inside.”

facts.fact: 他眯眼：不信她的表演、但也没打发她
facts.anchor: Harrison narrowed his eyes. He wasn’t buying my act, but he wasn’t dismissing me, either.

facts.fact: 几秒的权衡：嫌陪她浪费时间 vs 能换到信息——他说「好」
facts.anchor: presumably enough time to weigh the annoyance of wasting time with me against the information he’d get

facts.fact: 出门时 Nova 把嘴唇抿成一道薄笑
facts.anchor: Nova pressed her lips into a thin smile on our way out.

facts.fact: 他们走向 Nova 宣布禁入的那几扇门；Harrison 从腰带环取钥匙
facts.anchor: Harrison pulled a key off his belt loop ring and opened one of them

facts.fact: 他说明进入的是 processing spaces——宰杀与剥皮的正式说法
facts.anchor: we were entering the processing spaces—the official term for alligator killing and skinning

facts.fact: 走廊宽阔明亮，淡淡漂白水味；逐间报名：屠宰、剥皮、腌皮、皮仓
facts.anchor: He named each room as we passed it: slaughtering room, skinning room, skin salting, skin storage.

facts.fact: 他说露趾鞋不能进去、不安全；并对她的人字拖 grimaced：恶心、很多液体
facts.anchor: “You can’t go inside with open-toed shoes. Not safe.” He grimaced at my flip-flops.

facts.fact: 她盘算：不懂真正的养殖就没法说服 Gazzie 让她继承；也许 Harrison 怕的正是这个
facts.anchor: I wouldn’t be able to convince Gazzie to let me inherit if I didn’t know anything about actual farming. Maybe that was what Harrison was afraid of.

facts.fact: 她压下自尊、摆出最沮丧的表情
facts.anchor: I repressed my pride, adopted my most dejected expression

facts.fact: 他说：若你不娇气，可以偷看屠宰间，那是唯一有窗的房
facts.anchor: “We can peek in the slaughtering room if you’re not squeamish. It’s the only room with windows.”

facts.fact: 他赌她会恶心，笑的是他：她多年画死掉腐烂的动物
facts.anchor: the joke was on him; I’d been drawing dead and decaying animals for years

facts.fact: 她贴上担忧的表情说试试
facts.anchor: I plastered on a worried expression and said I’d give it a try.

facts.fact: 屠宰间在走廊最末、旁边一扇门大概通向室外
facts.anchor: The slaughtering room was the last one down the hallway, beside a door that presumably led outside

facts.fact: 两扇大窗配敞开的乙烯基百叶，里面看得清楚
facts.anchor: Two large windows covered with open vinyl blinds provided a clear view inside.

facts.fact: 约为两间教室大小、水泥墙与水泥地坡向中央排水口
facts.anchor: About double the size of a school classroom, it had concrete walls and floors that sloped to a center drain

facts.fact: 天花板右后角有一道旧漏水的痕迹顺墙而下
facts.anchor: In the far-right ceiling corner, the telltale mark of an old leak trailed down the wall.

facts.fact: 门上方又挂着 Ida 主画像的一份拷贝
facts.anchor: My eyes shot above the door, where another copy of Ida’s primary portrait hung.

facts.fact: 只看得见她精致的鞋尖从草里露出
facts.anchor: I could just see her delicate shoes poking out of the grass.

facts.fact: 她说好莱坞可以拿这里当砍杀片布景
facts.anchor: “Yeah, Hollywood could use this as a slasher film set.”

facts.fact: 他：等着瞧
facts.anchor: “Just wait,” he said.

facts.fact: 她没看错——他的脸泛青；也许他才是那个娇气的人
facts.anchor: If I wasn’t mistaken—and I wasn’t—his face was tinged green. Maybe he was the squeamish one.

facts.fact: 她补一句：不像个未来屠宰业老板该有的样子
facts.anchor: Not a great look for a future slaughtering-business owner.

facts.fact: 门被撞开：Gazzie 与昨天那个瘦的山羊胡男人拖进一条鳄鱼，嘴被管道胶带缠住
facts.anchor: Gazzie and the thin goateed man I’d seen the day before hauled in an alligator, its mouth bound with duct tape.

facts.fact: 叙述者惊讶于她还穿着来时那套白衬衫牛仔裤
facts.anchor: To my surprise, she still wore the jeans and white button-down shirt she’d arrived in.

facts.fact: 两人本可以从窗外看见他们，要么太专注要么决定无视
facts.anchor: They both could have seen Harrison and me outside the window, but were either too focused to notice or decided to ignore us.

facts.fact: 他们把鳄鱼制在排水口上方后，Gazzie 走到角落拿起棒球棒
facts.anchor: Once they wrestled the alligator above the drain, she strode to the corner and picked up a baseball bat.

facts.fact: 毫无仪式地举过鳄鱼头顶砸下，血喷在她衬衫上
facts.anchor: Without any fanfare, she raised it above the alligator’s head and slammed it down, blood spraying across her shirt.

facts.fact: 鳄鱼不动了但眼是睁的——它只是被打晕
facts.anchor: The alligator stopped moving, but its eyes were open. It was stunned.

facts.fact: Gazzie 挥手让那人出去；那人离开时嘴唇厌恶地蜷起
facts.anchor: As he left, his lip curled in disgust.

facts.fact: 来不及分析他的表情，Gazzie 已到鳄鱼身后、手里有刀
facts.anchor: Before I could analyze his expression, Gazzie moved behind the alligator, knife in hand.

facts.fact: Harrison 小声问她确定受得了
facts.anchor: Harrison turned his head to me. “Sure you can handle this?” he whispered.

facts.fact: 她反问：你确定你可以
facts.anchor: “Sure you can?” I countered.

facts.fact: 他哼了一声：她戳到了软处
facts.anchor: He grunted. I’d hit a weak spot.

facts.fact: Gazzie 背对他们但看得够清；移动时衬衫从裤里脱出
facts.anchor: Gazzie’s back was to us, but I could see well enough. Shirt untucking as she moved

facts.fact: 刀插进头顶再横拉；鳄鱼扑腾几下便静止
facts.anchor: she held the knife over the alligator and plunged it into the top of its head, yanking it to the side. The alligator thrashed a few times before it stilled.

facts.fact: 她为这 sudden violence 皱眉却移不开眼
facts.anchor: I winced at the sudden violence but couldn’t tear my eyes away.

facts.fact: 比喻：她关掉一条鳄鱼像别人从玩具里拔电池一样轻松
facts.anchor: She’d shut down the alligator as easily as anyone else might pull a battery out of a toy.

facts.fact: Harrison 低声解释：她在切断脊髓
facts.anchor: “She’s severing the spinal cord,” Harrison whispered, startling me.

facts.fact: 本该用 captive bolt 确认死亡，但 Gazzie 很准
facts.anchor: “We should make sure it’s dead with a captive bolt, but Gazzie is pretty accurate.”

facts.fact: 他的语气——略带厌恶、略带愧疚——让她停顿
facts.anchor: His tone—slightly disgusted, slightly guilty—gave me pause.

facts.fact: 解释：像枪，但射出一根金属杆穿过头骨、痛苦更少；他们有，但 Gazzie 说不传统
facts.anchor: It’s like a gun, but it fires a metal rod through an animal’s skull. It’s less painful. We have one, but Gazzie says it’s not traditional, so.

facts.fact: 她胃一紧：她当着腿边擦刀
facts.anchor: My stomach clenched as I watched her wipe the knife on her leg.

facts.fact: 她的两问：她在不在乎弄疼它／还是早就不想了
facts.anchor: Did she care that she was hurting the alligator? Or did she simply not think about it anymore?

facts.fact: 她猜想 Savannah 的同事能否说出祖母肯定违反的具体法规；大概不能
facts.anchor: I wondered if my coworkers in Savannah could name the exact regulations my grandmother was surely violating. Probably not.

facts.fact: 她想：鳄鱼不够可爱，活动家不会注意；但临终大概和别的农场动物一样——害怕、孤独
facts.anchor: Alligators weren’t cute enough for activists to notice, though they were probably like any other farm animal when facing their deaths—scared, alone.

facts.fact: 她自我提醒：自己不是鳄鱼专家，它们甚至可能不像人那样感受疼痛
facts.anchor: I reminded myself I wasn’t an alligator expert. They might not even feel pain like humans.

facts.fact: 她推测农场一定没被常规检查；血在腿上积、腿发痒想动
facts.anchor: “The farm must not get regular inspections,” I mused, shifting uncomfortably. Blood was pooling in my legs

facts.fact: 他纠正：州渔业野生动物委员会与农业部消费者服务局常来检查
facts.anchor: We get them pretty frequently from the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services.

facts.fact: 但 Gazzie 从线人提前得到通知，检查时她规矩得很
facts.anchor: But Gazzie gets a heads-up from her contacts, so when they’re around, she’s on her best behavior.

facts.fact: 他嘴角抽出一个讽刺的笑：Greer 家在这片太久了、州里最老的农场之一，随之有一定宽容度、上面有朋友
facts.anchor: “The Greers have been around forever. One of the oldest farms in the state. There’s a certain amount of leniency that comes with that. Friends in high places and all.”

facts.fact: 她说：不知她会不会重新考虑宰杀流程
facts.anchor: “I wonder if she’d reconsider the slaughtering process.”

facts.fact: 他嗤：没门
facts.anchor: He scoffed. “Not a chance.”

facts.fact: 她带着自己没有的信心回嘴：也许是没被合适的人请求
facts.anchor: With a confidence I didn’t feel, I retorted, “Maybe the right person hasn’t asked her.”

facts.fact: 他翻白眼打发她；她却认真，已在想若自己接手要怎么改造农场
facts.anchor: Harrison rolled his eyes, dismissing me, but I was in earnest, already brainstorming ways I could update the farm if I took over.

facts.fact: Gazzie 起身时鳄鱼无力地挪前爪——还没死、差一点
facts.anchor: When Gazzie stood, the alligator feebly moved its foot forward. It wasn’t dead. Not quite.

facts.fact: 她骂了一句抓起棒球棒；那可怜的东西拖着身子逃，她跟到墙边再砸过头顶
facts.anchor: The pathetic beast dragged itself along the floor, trying to escape, but she followed it to the wall, lifted the baseball bat, and slammed it over its head.

facts.fact: 然后她又把棒子举起来
facts.anchor: Then she raised it again.

facts.fact: 她身体前倾、鼻尖撞在玻璃上：鳄鱼的里面长什么样？
facts.anchor: I leaned forward, nose bumping the glass. What did alligators look like inside?

facts.fact: 妈妈的声音在耳里 ghosted：你最好把你心里那个魔鬼驯住
facts.anchor: Mama’s voice ghosted in my ear. You’d better tame that devil in you.

facts.fact: 她闭眼后退；不想知道继续看下去会是什么感觉、不想让妈妈的话成真、不想成为她眼里那个扭曲的人
facts.anchor: Closing my eyes, I stepped backward. I didn’t want to know what I’d feel if I kept watching, didn’t want her words to be true

facts.fact: 她的自我形象：被黑暗拽着的狂暴生物
facts.anchor: didn’t want to be the twisted person she believed I was—a raging creature drawn to darkness.

facts.fact: Harrison 吐气时她睁眼：Gazzie 从墙上取下软管冲地；紫红的水旋进排水口
facts.anchor: Gazzie pulled a hose off the wall and sprayed the floor. Puce-red water swirled into the drain.

facts.fact: 接下来的流程：躯体送去剥皮、皮腌制、肉交给屠宰队
facts.anchor: “They’ll take the body to skinning. Then the hide cures while the meat goes to the butchering team.”

facts.fact: 她追问骨头去哪；他反问什么意思
facts.anchor: “And where do the bones go?”

facts.fact: 问出口才明白：那是妈妈衣橱墙上追着她的那句——Greer 家的财富建在鳄鱼骨头上
facts.anchor: I’d asked the question before realizing why: It was the phrase on Mama’s closet wall, haunting me

facts.fact: 她说没见过骨堆、问是不是磨掉
facts.anchor: “I haven’t seen a pile of them anywhere. Do you grind them up?”

facts.fact: 他：头骨留一部分、其余扔掉；再几次深呼吸后语气粗硬：演出结束了 Miss Greer
facts.anchor: “We keep some of the skulls and trash the rest.” After a few more deep breaths, he spoke again, voice gruff.

facts.fact: 她心不在焉地纠正：我姓 Beaumont
facts.anchor: “It’s Beaumont,” I said absently.

facts.fact: 她不想让 Harrison 以为能支使她，但骗到他带看加工区已算赢
facts.anchor: I didn’t want Harrison to think he could order me around, but I’d already won by tricking him into showing me the processing facility.

facts.fact: 他说完就转身要走、她跟着动，眼睛仍留在屠宰间
facts.anchor: He turned to go, and I made to follow, eyes still on the slaughtering room.

facts.fact: Gazzie 转向 Ida Greer 的画像；有一息——只一息——她低下头，像在祈祷
facts.anchor: Gazzie had turned to face Ida Greer’s portrait. For a breath—only a breath, no longer—she bowed her head, like she was praying.

relations: Harrison 与 Nova：她半笑僵住、被疑为「想独占他」或「受命监视」；两种解释并列未裁
Perhaps she liked to keep Harrison to herself.
